subject: Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: Before using a disc grinder to remove rust from a car door sill, an apprentice in Aba should FIRST put on
options: a pair of rubber boots and a cap only
questions.explanation: Grinding throws out sparks and abrasive particles, so eye protection comes first.

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: Empty paint and thinner tins in a spray shop should be disposed of by
options: placing them in a labelled hazardous-waste container for collection
pouring the residue into a drain and selling the empty tins to traders
keeping them under the spray booth floor grating
questions.explanation: Paint and solvent residues are hazardous waste; they are kept in marked containers for licensed collection or recycling.

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: Which of these is a WORKSHOP-KEEPING cause of accidents?
options: A tired worker using a cutting disc
Air hoses left lying across the walkway
Working while under the influence of alcohol
questions.explanation: Hoses left across walkways are a housekeeping fault that causes trips; the others are human factors.

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: A grinding machine guard is found cracked during work. The correct action is to
options: switch off, tag the machine "out of use" and report it to the supervisor
tape the crack and continue working carefully
remove the guard completely so that it cannot fall off
use the machine only for small jobs until the end of the week
ask another apprentice to finish the job on it
questions.explanation: Faulty machines must be isolated, labelled and reported so that nobody else uses them before repair.

questions.stem: Which hand tool is used to reach behind an inner panel and spread the force of a hammer blow over a wide area?
questions.explanation: A body spoon is a flat, curved bar used as a dolly in confined places or to spread a blow.

questions.stem: One DISADVANTAGE of using power tools rather than hand tools in a body shop is that power tools
options: always do the work more slowly than skilled hand work
produce a poorer finish on every job
cannot be used on steel panels
require more physical effort from the worker
cost more to buy and need a steady electricity supply
questions.explanation: Power tools are faster but are expensive and depend on electricity or compressed air, which is a real cost in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Replacing a worn air compressor belt only after it has snapped is an example of
questions.explanation: Corrective (breakdown) maintenance is carried out after a fault has occurred.

questions.stem: Measuring the vibration level of a compressor motor every month so that its bearings can be changed just before they fail is
questions.explanation: Predictive maintenance uses condition monitoring (vibration, temperature, noise) to forecast when a part will fail.

questions.topic: Materials for Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: In body solder marked 30/70, the figures refer to the percentages of
questions.explanation: Body solder is a tin-lead alloy; 30/70 means 30% tin and 70% lead.

questions.topic: Materials for Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: Which of the following is an UNDERCOAT material?
questions.explanation: Primers, fillers and sealers are undercoats; lacquers and enamels are top coats.

questions.topic: Materials for Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem: A painter needs 1.2 litres of ready-to-spray paint mixed in the ratio paint : thinner = 3 : 1. The volume of paint required is
questions.explanation: Paint = 3/4 x 1.2 = 0.9 litre; thinner = 0.3 litre.

questions.stem: Which metal in the list below contains no iron?
questions.explanation: Brass is a copper-zinc alloy and contains no iron.

questions.stem: A panel beater shapes a flat steel blank into a curved wing by repeated blows without it splitting. The property of steel that makes this possible is
questions.explanation: Malleability is the ability to be deformed by hammering or rolling without breaking.

questions.stem: Cast iron is NOT used for car body panels mainly because it is
options: too soft to hold a shape
questions.explanation: Cast iron cannot be pressed into thin panels and would crack on impact; it is used for engine blocks instead.

questions.stem: Heating steel and allowing it to cool very slowly in the furnace to make it soft is called
questions.explanation: Annealing softens steel and relieves stress through slow furnace cooling.

questions.stem: After hardening a cold chisel, it is reheated to a lower temperature and cooled. The purpose of this second process is to
options: make the chisel fully soft again
increase the carbon content of the surface
remove the scale from the surface
change the steel to cast iron
reduce brittleness while keeping much of the hardness
questions.explanation: Tempering reduces the brittleness left by hardening, giving toughness.

questions.stem: A low-carbon steel part that needs a hard, wear-resistant outer skin but a tough core should be
questions.explanation: Case-hardening adds carbon to the surface layer, which is then hardened, leaving a tough core.

questions.stem: Acetylene cylinders must always be used standing upright because
options: the gas is heavier than air
the valve only opens in that position
the acetone in them could otherwise be drawn out with the gas
the regulator gauge reads wrongly when lying down
the oxygen in the other cylinder would leak backwards into the acetylene
questions.explanation: Acetylene is dissolved in acetone; a lying cylinder can discharge liquid acetone into the regulator and torch.

questions.stem: Small gas holes trapped in a weld bead are a defect known as
questions.explanation: Porosity is gas pockets in the weld, often caused by dirty metal or wrong flame setting.

questions.stem: The main difference between the high-pressure and low-pressure oxy-acetylene systems is that in the low-pressure system
options: oxygen is supplied at low pressure from a generator
no regulators are used on the oxygen cylinder
the flame temperature is much higher
acetylene is supplied from a generator at low pressure and an injector-type blowpipe is used
only propane can be used as fuel gas
questions.explanation: The low-pressure system takes acetylene from a generator; the injector blowpipe uses the oxygen stream to draw in the acetylene.

questions.stem: A vehicle whose body and chassis are made as one unit is said to have
questions.explanation: In integral construction the body shell itself carries the loads; there is no separate chassis.

questions.stem: A stretched area on a bonnet that has been over-hammered is best brought back to shape by
options: more hammering of the area on a dolly until it is level again
filling with thick body filler only
heat-shrinking with a torch and quenching
questions.explanation: Shrinking with heat and rapid cooling draws the stretched metal back; filler would only hide it.

questions.stem: Hammering ON-dolly means that the
options: dolly is held a short distance to one side of the blow
panel is hammered without any support
hammer and dolly strike each other through a hole
dolly is held directly behind the spot being struck
dolly is used as a hammer
questions.explanation: On-dolly work raises low spots and smooths metal by squeezing it between hammer and dolly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a MAJOR body section of a car?
options: The door handle and its locking rod
questions.explanation: Body sections are the front (engine) compartment, the passenger section and the rear section.

questions.stem: The basic alignment principle in major collision repair is that the damaged structure should be pulled
options: in the same direction as the impact force
in the opposite direction to that of the impact force
only by hammering from inside the passenger compartment of the car
only after all panels have been painted
questions.explanation: Pulling opposite to the force of impact reverses the damage sequence, so the structure returns to its dimensions.

questions.stem: A tram gauge is used in major body repair to
options: measure the thickness of the paint film on every panel after spraying
check point-to-point measurements of the body against the manufacturer's data
test the pressure of the body jack
questions.explanation: A tram (tracking) gauge compares diagonal and length measurements between reference holes with the body dimension chart.

questions.stem: Aluminium panels should be worked with tools that
options: are kept separate from those used on steel
are slightly rusty, because the rust gives a better grip on the soft metal
questions.explanation: Steel particles embedded from shared tools cause galvanic corrosion on aluminium.

questions.stem: Compared with steel, aluminium panels are harder to repair because aluminium
options: is heavier than steel and rusts much faster in damp weather
work-hardens quickly and gives no colour change before it melts
has a very high melting point
questions.explanation: Aluminium becomes hard and cracks when worked and does not glow before melting, so heat must be controlled carefully.

questions.stem: When straightening a dented aluminium deck lid with heat, the temperature can be controlled by
options: waiting for the metal to glow dull red before starting to work it
touching the panel with bare fingers
using temperature-indicating crayon or paint on the panel
questions.explanation: Since aluminium does not change colour, heat-indicating crayons or a thermometer are used to avoid overheating.

questions.stem: A bumper material that becomes soft every time hot air is applied, so that a filler rod can be fused into it, is
options: a glass fibre mat soaked in resin
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics re-soften on heating, so they can be repaired by melting (plastic welding).

questions.stem: A precaution when repairing plastic bumpers by melting is to
options: work in a ventilated area because heated plastic gives off fumes
use the highest possible flame to finish quickly
keep the bumper wet during welding
cover the work with paper while heating
questions.explanation: Overheated plastics release toxic fumes, so ventilation and correct temperature are essential.

questions.stem: In glass fibre panel repair, the resin is made to set by adding
questions.explanation: Polyester resin cures by chemical reaction when a catalyst/hardener is mixed in.

questions.stem: In a gravity-feed spray gun the paint cup is placed
questions.explanation: Gravity guns have the cup on top so that paint flows down to the nozzle by its own weight.

questions.stem: Which part of a spray gun controls the amount of paint leaving the nozzle?
questions.explanation: The fluid needle seats in the fluid tip; adjusting its travel varies the paint flow.

questions.stem: Before priming bare steel, the surface should be cleaned with
questions.explanation: Wax and grease remover leaves the surface free of contamination that would stop adhesion.

questions.stem: Feather-edging during surface preparation means
options: removing all paint with paint stripper
sanding the edge of the old paint to a smooth taper
applying masking tape around the panel
questions.explanation: Feather-edging tapers the broken paint edge so that no ridge shows through the new finish.

questions.stem: The manufacturer's paint code on a vehicle identification plate is important because it
options: allows the exact original colour to be mixed
shows the year the car was made
tells the thickness of the body panels
questions.explanation: The paint code identifies the formula of the factory colour so it can be matched.

questions.stem: A paint that dries mainly by evaporation of its solvent and can be re-dissolved by its thinner is
questions.explanation: Lacquers dry by solvent evaporation and remain soluble in thinner; enamels cure by chemical change.

questions.stem: In metallic paint, a WET spray application tends to make the colour look
options: lighter, because the flakes lie flat near the surface
exactly the same as a dry coat
darker, because the flakes sink and lie unevenly
questions.explanation: In a wet coat the flakes sink and tilt, giving a darker shade; dry spraying holds flakes flat at the top and looks lighter.

questions.stem: Mr Okon wants to open a panel-beating and spray shop in Uyo. Which consideration matters MOST in picking the plot?
options: Nearness to a primary school and a church
Easy access for customers and vehicles
questions.explanation: A body shop needs easy road access so damaged vehicles can be brought in and customers can reach it.

questions.topic: Safety Rules and Regulations in Auto Body Repairs and Spray Painting
questions.stem:
(a) Define safety rules and regulations as used in an auto body workshop. [3 marks]
(b) List four items of personal protective equipment for a spray painter and state the use of each. [8 marks]
(c) State four ways of keeping the workshop floor safe. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) rules/codes of conduct to prevent accidents, injury and damage to people, equipment and environment
2 marks: (b) respirator/nose mask: protects lungs from paint mist and fumes
2 marks: (b) goggles: protects eyes from spray and particles
2 marks: (b) overall/spray suit: protects body and clothes
2 marks: (b) gloves/boots/ear defenders with correct use
4 marks: (c) any four: clean spills with sawdust/dry sand; keep hoses and cables off walkways; store tools after use; remove scraps; keep gangways clear; good lighting (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Safety rules are laid-down codes that guide workers to avoid accidents. A spray painter needs a respirator (lungs), goggles (eyes), overalls (body), gloves (skin from solvents). Floors are kept safe by cleaning spills with sawdust, keeping hoses tidy, clearing scraps and marking gangways.

questions.stem:
(a) Name five items of equipment that make up a high-pressure oxy-acetylene welding plant. [5 marks]
(b) Describe the procedure for setting up and lighting the blowpipe. [6 marks]
(c) State two causes and one remedy each for slag inclusion and lack of penetration in a weld. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) oxygen cylinder, acetylene cylinder, regulators, hoses, blowpipe/nozzle, flashback arrestors, spark lighter (any five)
1 mark: (b) crack (blow out) cylinder valves to remove dirt
1 mark: (b) fit regulators and hoses with correct threads (left-hand for acetylene)
1 mark: (b) set working pressures for the nozzle size
1 mark: (b) check for leaks with soapy water
1 mark: (b) open acetylene slightly and light with spark lighter
1 mark: (b) open oxygen and adjust to neutral flame
2 marks: (c) slag inclusion: dirty surface or poor technique; remedy clean metal between runs
2 marks: (c) lack of penetration: low heat/fast travel/small nozzle; remedy larger nozzle, slower travel, correct gap
questions.explanation: The plant comprises two cylinders, regulators, colour-coded hoses, flashback arrestors and the blowpipe. Set-up: crack valves, fit regulators, attach hoses, set pressures, leak test, light acetylene, add oxygen to neutral. Slag inclusion from dirt — clean properly; lack of penetration from too little heat — increase heat/slow down.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between integral and composite body construction. [4 marks]
(b) Describe how a shallow dent on a car door may be repaired using hammer and dolly, pull taps and heat-shrinking. [8 marks]
(c) State three tools used in minor body repairs. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) integral: body and frame form one welded unit carrying loads
2 marks: (a) composite: separate chassis frame with body bolted on
2 marks: (b) assess damage, remove trim, clean paint from area
2 marks: (b) pull taps/stud puller welded or attached and pulled to raise the low area
2 marks: (b) hammer and dolly (on/off dolly) to smooth highs and lows
2 marks: (b) heat-shrink stretched spots with torch and quench; check with file/hand
3 marks: (c) any three: body hammer, dolly, spoon, pry bar, slide hammer, body file (1 each)
questions.explanation: Integral bodies have no separate chassis; composite bodies are bolted to a frame. A shallow dent is cleaned, pulled out with pull taps or a slide hammer, worked with hammer and dolly, and any stretched metal is heat-shrunk before filing and finishing.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain how paint reaches the nozzle in a gravity gun, a siphon gun and a pressure-feed gun. [6 marks]
(b) A customer's gun is giving a pattern that is heavy at the top and light at the bottom. Name five parts of the gun you would examine or clean. [5 marks]
(c) Give four rules for handling a spray gun during and after a job. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) gravity gun: cup above, paint flows by gravity
2 marks: (a) suction/siphon gun: cup below, paint drawn up by vacuum
2 marks: (a) pressure-feed gun: paint forced from pressurised pot/tank
5 marks: (b) any five: air cap, fluid tip, fluid needle, trigger, air valve, gun body, cup, spreader adjuster, fluid adjuster (1 each)
4 marks: (c) any four: hold gun perpendicular at correct distance; overlap strokes by about half; never point at people; clean immediately after use; use correct pressure; wear respirator (1 each)
questions.explanation: Gravity, suction and pressure-feed guns differ in how paint reaches the nozzle. Parts include air cap, fluid tip and needle, trigger, air valve and body. Precautions: correct distance and angle, overlap, clean after use, correct pressure, protective equipment.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between thermoplastic and thermosetting plastics, giving one example of each used on vehicles. [6 marks]
(b) Outline the steps for repairing a cracked thermoplastic bumper by melting (plastic welding). [6 marks]
(c) State three precautions when working with plastics and resins. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) thermoplastic softens on reheating, can be welded
1 mark: (a) example: polypropylene/ABS/PVC bumper
2 marks: (a) thermosetting sets permanently, cannot be remelted
1 mark: (a) example: polyester/epoxy resin, GRP panels
1 mark: (b) identify the plastic type (ISO code)
1 mark: (b) clean and V-groove the crack
1 mark: (b) align and clamp/tack the edges
2 marks: (b) melt matching filler rod into groove with hot-air welder at correct temperature
1 mark: (b) allow to cool, sand and finish
3 marks: (c) any three: ventilation, gloves, eye protection, avoid overheating, no naked flame near resin (1 each)
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics soften repeatedly (PP bumpers); thermosets cure permanently (GRP). Repair: identify, clean, groove, align, weld with matching rod, cool and finish. Precautions: ventilation, gloves, goggles, correct temperature.

questions.stem:
Ada has finished her apprenticeship and wants to set up her own panel-beating and spray shop.
(a) Advise her on five things she should consider before choosing where to site the shop. [5 marks]
(b) Prepare a list of six tools or items of equipment she must buy first. [6 marks]
(c) Suggest four ways she can win and keep customers. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) any five: capital, accessibility, land/space, electricity/water supply, nearness to customers, government regulations, security (1 each)
6 marks: (b) any six: air compressor, spray gun, hammers and dollies, welding set, grinder, sander, body jack, spray booth (1 each)
4 marks: (c) any four: quality work, keeping to delivery dates, fair prices, good customer relations, advertising, warranty (1 each)
questions.explanation: Location depends on capital, access, space, power, customers and regulations. Starting equipment includes compressor, guns, hammers and dollies, welding set, grinder and sander. Good work, punctuality, fair price and advertising retain customers.
